title: Deterministic network & streaming fixture harness for SDK contract tests
text:
Deterministic network & streaming fixture harness for SDK contract tests

description:
Goal: Deliver a deterministic fixture + mock-proxy harness that lets SDK teams (Python, TypeScript, Go) write reliable VCR-style recordings and contract tests against the Redwood API while simulating realistic network conditions (latency envelopes, packet loss, half-closed streams, backpressure).

Problem: Our current VCR/record-replay artifacts capture happy-path token streams but fail to exercise streaming edge cases (mid-stream errors, slow clients, TCP stalls) and retry/idempotency behavior. That causes flakiness in CI and missed regressions in streaming ergonomics and retry semantics across SDKs.

Approach:
- Implement a lightweight deterministic proxy (Go) that can:
  * Replay recorded server responses with fine-grained control over inter-chunk delays and chunk boundaries (HTTP/1.1 chunking + SSE + HTTP/2 frames).
  * Inject configurable failure modes: connection reset, 4xx/5xx mid-stream, deliberate header truncation, TLS handshake delay.
  * Support deterministic RNG seeds and a synthetic clock so replays are bit-for-bit reproducible.
- Provide language bindings/tests:
  * python-fixture-cli: record + shrink + annotate cassette metadata (SDK version, model, prompt).
  * ts-proxy-shim: lightweight node proxy wrapper for TS SDK CI usage.
  * go-playback: small harness for Go SDK unit/integration tests.
- Define a cassette schema v2 that records: request/response frames, per-chunk timing, connection events, randomized-but-reproducible latencies, and server-assigned tokens for idempotency verification.
- Create contract assertions: golden-structure snapshot for stream messages, retry-count and backoff timing bounds, idempotency header checks.
- CI integration: add a "cassette-verified" Jest/PyTest/Gotest job that runs recorded scenarios plus randomized stress permutations (seeded) and fails the pipeline if flakiness rate > 0.5% over N=100 runs.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term storage of cassettes in artifact registry, recorder UI, and private deployment (VPC) network emulation (will be follow-ups).

acceptance_criteria:
Proxy service (go) can replay cassette v2 files with deterministic timing on developer machines and CI
Tooling to record and shrink fixtures exists for Python and TypeScript and is documented
Three canonical streaming scenarios added to SDK test suites (slow-client, mid-stream-500, abrupt-reset) for Python/TS/Go
CI gate job added; baseline flakiness measured and documented; threshold set and enforced
Contract assertions validate retry behavior and idempotency headers; at least one bug found/fixed by this harness

comments:
2026-02-02 - Avery Chen: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Decided to standardize on cassette v2 JSON to support chunk timing and connection events. (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/SDK+Deterministic+Fixtures)
2026-02-05 - Ravi Kapoor: Prototype of Go proxy started (branch: feat/fixture-proxy). Basic replay with fixed chunk delays working locally. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-proxy/pull/47
2026-02-07 - Sofia Martinez (SDK lead): Requested that the cassette metadata include SDK version and model checksum to avoid stale recordings across runtime changes. Added to schema v2 draft.
2026-02-09 - Ravi Kapoor: Integrated synthetic clock for deterministic scheduling; found a race in Python recorder when shrinking cassettes — filed ENG-78103 as a follow-up to harden shrinker.
2026-02-11 - Design review (Emily Park): Reviewed streaming chunk UX for SDKs; suggested an ergonomic helper in TS to expose chunk boundaries to callers (will be tracked in ENG-78104).
2026-02-13 - Code review (PR #47): Feedback to add telemetry tags for scenario-name and seed. Added tests for 'abrupt-reset' scenario. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-proxy/pull/47
2026-02-14 - Ravi Kapoor: CI job draft submitted (pipeline: sdk-cassette-verify). Early runs show Python stream tests are stable; TS harness needs minor timeout adjustments. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-sdk/cassette-verification
